scr_gl_accrual_workbench.purpose: Shows the accruals RealPage has calculated from accrual templates — invoices-not-received estimates based on a vendor's prior invoices, utility management pending exports, recurring service contracts — so the accountant can review each suggestion, adjust amounts, and post the month-end accrual entries with auto-reversal.
scr_gl_accrual_workbench.outcome: A reviewed, system-assisted month-end accrual batch (DR expense / CR 2020 Accrued Expenses, reversing on day 1 of the next month) that captures unbilled costs without building every accrual by hand.
scr_gl_accrual_workbench.rootCause: Across a portfolio, the same unbilled costs recur every month: water/sewer billed 45 days in arrears, trash, landscaping, pest control, elevator contracts. Estimating each in Excel per property wastes hours and produces inconsistent methods. Templates plus a workbench standardize the method (e.g., prior-3-month average) and leave the accountant to review exceptions.
scr_gl_accrual_workbench.ifSkipped: Month-end expenses are understated, NOI is overstated, and the next month's actual invoices create unexplained spikes; if suggestions are posted without review, stale templates generate accruals for vendors no longer under contract.
gaap: ASC 450-20 — accrue probable, estimable incurred costs
Accrual-basis matching of expense to period of service
redFlags: Accrual posted for a vendor whose actual invoice was already entered for the same period (double expense)
Suggested amounts accepted even when the vendor's prior invoices included one-time charges
Accruals posted without an auto-reverse date

scr_gl_adding_a_gaap_compliance_adjustin.purpose: Posts an adjusting entry to a specific non-operational book — the GAAP (compliance) book or the Tax book — so that differences between the property's everyday accrual book and GAAP or tax reporting (straight-line rent, ASC 842 lease entries, tax depreciation, capitalization differences) are recorded without disturbing the operating financials.
scr_gl_adding_a_gaap_compliance_adjustin.outcome: GAAP- or tax-basis financial statements that differ from the management book only by documented adjusting entries, with the operating (accrual) book left unchanged for the property team.
scr_gl_adding_a_gaap_compliance_adjustin.rootCause: Institutional owners frequently report on several bases: the management-company accrual book for NOI, a GAAP book for audited fund financials, and a tax book for partnership returns (MACRS depreciation, §263(a) repair vs capital rules). Keeping adjustments in separate books is how one ledger serves all three audiences.
scr_gl_adding_a_gaap_compliance_adjustin.ifSkipped: GAAP or tax adjustments get booked into the operating book (distorting NOI and budget variances) or live only in spreadsheets outside the system, making audited statements hard to reproduce and book-tax differences hard to support on the K-1.
gaap: ASC 842-30 — straight-line lessor income for commercial leases
ASC 360 vs IRC §168 — book/tax depreciation differences
ASC 740 — book-tax differences (if the entity is taxable)
redFlags: Adjusting entry posted to the operating accrual book by mistake
Adjustments not reversed or rolled forward consistently each year
No workpaper supporting the difference between books

scr_gl_adding_a_journal_entry.purpose: Creates a manual general journal entry for anything that does not flow through A/P, A/R or another subledger — reclassifications of mis-coded invoices, month-end accruals, payroll allocations, lender escrow activity, GPR and loss-to-lease postings, intercompany charges — saved as draft for review or posted directly.
scr_gl_adding_a_journal_entry.outcome: A balanced, documented GL entry with a description and attached support that updates the trial balance and flows to the owner's financial statements.
scr_gl_adding_a_journal_entry.rootCause: Subledgers only capture routine transactions. Everything else — corrections, estimates, allocations, servicer-driven loan activity — must be recorded manually. Manual JEs are also the highest-risk transactions for error and management override, which is why they need a controlled entry screen with draft, approval and support.
scr_gl_adding_a_journal_entry.ifSkipped: Accruals, reclasses and loan activity are missing, financial statements are misstated, and corrections are pushed into later months where they distort trends.
gaap: COSO 2013 / AU-C 240 — manual journal entries as a management-override fraud risk
redFlags: JEs posted to subledger control accounts (1210, 2010) that break the subledger tie-out
Round-dollar JEs with vague descriptions like 'adjust' and no attachment
JEs posted by the same person who approves them
Entries dated in a closed or reported period

scr_gl_adding_a_prepaid_journal_entry.purpose: Sets up a prepaid schedule for a cost paid in advance — insurance premium, advance real estate tax installment, annual software license, service contract — so RealPage automatically posts the monthly amortization from 1310 Prepaid Expenses to the expense account over the benefit period.
scr_gl_adding_a_prepaid_journal_entry.outcome: A scheduled series of monthly entries (DR expense / CR 1310) that expense the prepayment evenly over its term, with the remaining balance visible at any month-end.
scr_gl_adding_a_prepaid_journal_entry.rootCause: Large prepayments paid in one month benefit many months. Without an automated schedule, accountants either forget to amortize (overstating assets) or compute amounts inconsistently each month. The prepaid setup ties the amortization to the original payment.
scr_gl_adding_a_prepaid_journal_entry.ifSkipped: The full premium sits in 1310 or is expensed on payment, creating NOI swings, inaccurate BVA reporting and prepaid balances that cannot be supported at audit.
gaap: ASC 340-10 — prepaid costs deferred and expensed over the benefit period
redFlags: Schedule term does not match the policy period (e.g., 12 months set for a 13-month policy)
Start month set to the payment month instead of the coverage start
Mid-term policy cancellations not reflected in the schedule

scr_gl_adding_an_accrual_template_for_in.purpose: Defines a reusable accrual rule that looks at a vendor's prior invoices for a property and GL account and calculates a month-end estimate when that month's invoice has not arrived — typical for water/sewer, gas, electric common-area, trash hauling and contract services.
scr_gl_adding_an_accrual_template_for_in.outcome: Consistent, rules-based accrual suggestions every month in the Accrual Workbench for the vendors most likely to bill late, instead of ad hoc estimates.
scr_gl_adding_an_accrual_template_for_in.rootCause: Utility and contract vendors bill in arrears on cycles that do not align to month-end. The same vendors need accruing every month, so encoding the method once (prior invoice average, last invoice amount) removes judgment variation between preparers and properties.
scr_gl_adding_an_accrual_template_for_in.ifSkipped: Accountants miss late-billing vendors or estimate them inconsistently, leading to expense swings, budget variance questions and audit challenges on the accrual method.
gaap: ASC 450-20 — reasonable estimation of incurred costs
ASC 250-10 — consistent application of estimation methods
redFlags: Templates referencing vendors whose contracts ended
Lookback period capturing a seasonal spike (summer electricity) for a winter month
Template account differs from where the actual invoice will be coded, so reversal and actual hit different lines

scr_gl_adding_an_accrual_template_for_re.purpose: Creates an accrual template that uses the RealPage Utility Management 'pending export' queue — utility bills received and processed by the utility management service but not yet exported to A/P — to accrue those costs at month-end.
scr_gl_adding_an_accrual_template_for_re.outcome: Utility invoices that are already known (received and audited by the utility service) but not yet in A/P are accrued at their actual amounts instead of an estimate.
scr_gl_adding_an_accrual_template_for_re.rootCause: Properties that outsource utility bill processing to RealPage Utility Management (and bill residents back through RUBS or submetering) often have a lag between bill receipt and A/P export. Accruing from that pending queue is more accurate than estimating from prior months and keeps utility expense aligned with the utility reimbursement income billed to residents.
scr_gl_adding_an_accrual_template_for_re.ifSkipped: Utility expense lags by a month while resident reimbursement income (4110) is billed on time, mismatching income and expense and distorting utility recovery ratios the asset manager tracks.
gaap: ASC 606 — utility reimbursements as variable consideration when billed to residents
redFlags: Pending bills accrued and also exported to A/P in the same period (double count)
Template only covering some utility types
Accruals not reversing when the export posts

scr_gl_allocations_overview.purpose: Explains RealPage's two allocation mechanisms — transaction allocations (splitting a single invoice or entry across properties or departments at entry) and G/L allocations (periodically redistributing pooled balances such as shared payroll, corporate insurance or regional office costs) — used to spread shared costs to the properties that consume them.
scr_gl_allocations_overview.outcome: Shared costs land on each property's P&L using a documented basis (units, square feet, revenue), so each property's NOI reflects its fair share and owners are charged correctly.
scr_gl_allocations_overview.rootCause: Management companies share staff, insurance programs, software and regional offices across many owners. Management agreements specify what can be charged back and on what basis; allocating incorrectly can over-charge one owner at another's expense, a contractual and fiduciary issue.
scr_gl_allocations_overview.ifSkipped: Shared costs remain in a pool or are charged on inconsistent bases, some owners subsidize others, and owner audits of reimbursable expenses produce disputes and refunds.
gaap: ASC 810 — intercompany allocations eliminated on consolidation
redFlags: Allocation basis (unit counts) not updated after a property acquisition or sale
Allocation percentages summing to more or less than 100%
Non-reimbursable corporate overhead allocated to owners

scr_gl_amortization.purpose: The curated workflow for creating recurring amortization schedules that expense multi-month prepaid costs — property insurance, software licenses, upfront loan fees — monthly and automatically instead of by hand.
scr_gl_amortization.outcome: Every material prepayment has a live schedule, monthly expense is smooth and predictable, and the 1310 balance equals the sum of unamortized schedules.
scr_gl_amortization.rootCause: Offshore teams handle dozens of properties, each with several prepaid items renewing on different dates. Manual monthly amortization is where items are forgotten; a schedule-driven approach turns it into a one-time setup with a monthly review.
scr_gl_amortization.ifSkipped: Prepaids are missed or double-amortized, insurance and tax lines swing unexpectedly, and the balance sheet carries expired prepaids.
gaap: ASC 835-30 — debt issuance costs amortized to interest expense
redFlags: Loan fees amortized to administrative expense instead of interest
Schedules continuing after the underlying policy was cancelled or the loan refinanced
Prepaid balance not tying to the sum of schedules

scr_gl_balance_sheet_report.purpose: Produces the property's balance sheet as of a period end — cash and restricted cash, resident receivables, prepaids and escrows, fixed assets net of depreciation, payables, accrued liabilities, security deposits, mortgage debt and equity — from the Financial Reports Library.
scr_gl_balance_sheet_report.outcome: The statement of financial position that goes into the owner package and that every balance-sheet reconciliation must support.
scr_gl_balance_sheet_report.rootCause: Owners, lenders and auditors judge the property's financial position and the quality of the books from the balance sheet: whether cash is real, liabilities are complete and debt is correctly stated. Balance-sheet reconciliations are the key month-end review for offshore teams because P&L errors eventually surface as unexplained balance-sheet balances.
scr_gl_balance_sheet_report.ifSkipped: Owners receive incomplete packages, balance-sheet errors (unreconciled cash, stale accruals, negative prepaid balances) go unnoticed, and lenders cannot verify reserve and escrow balances.
redFlags: Accounts with abnormal signs (credit balance in A/R, debit balance in A/P or accruals)
Balance-sheet accounts with no reconciliation in the work paper package
Balance sheet not balancing because of a current-year earnings roll issue

scr_gl_calculate_percentage_fees.purpose: Calculates the management fee (and other percentage-based fees such as asset management or incentive fees) as a percentage of the fee base defined in the management agreement — usually collected revenue or effective gross income — and generates the fee entry or payable.
scr_gl_calculate_percentage_fees.outcome: A correctly calculated monthly management fee (DR 6510 Management Fees / CR 2130 Due To Affiliates or 2010 Accounts Payable) that can be traced to the agreement's fee percentage and fee base.
scr_gl_calculate_percentage_fees.rootCause: Management fees (commonly 2-4% of collections) are the management company's own revenue, which creates a conflict of interest. Owners audit the calculation closely: which income lines are included (e.g., excluding security deposits, insurance proceeds, interest), cash vs accrual basis, and minimum fees. A system calculation with a defined base prevents both over-charging and under-billing.
scr_gl_calculate_percentage_fees.ifSkipped: Fees are calculated manually with the wrong base, owners discover over-charges in audits and claw back fees, or the management company under-bills and loses revenue.
gaap: ASC 850 — related-party transactions disclosure when the manager is an affiliate
redFlags: Fee base includes excluded items (security deposits, insurance proceeds, capital contributions)
Fee percentage differs from the current management agreement amendment
Fee paid on accrued revenue when the agreement specifies collections

scr_gl_close_books_page.purpose: Closes the books through a selected ending period so no application (A/P, A/R, Cash, GL, Fixed Assets) can post transactions dated on or before that date, freezing the reported financials.
scr_gl_close_books_page.outcome: A hard period lock across all modules, guaranteeing that reported numbers cannot be changed by backdated activity.
scr_gl_close_books_page.rootCause: RealPage lets users date transactions into earlier periods. Once financials are delivered to the owner, lender or auditor, any change breaks agreement with what was reported. Closing books is the strongest control against backdating by site teams, other accountants or integrations.
scr_gl_close_books_page.ifSkipped: Late invoices, resident adjustments or integration postings land in reported periods, the trial balance no longer matches the owner package, and next month's opening balances do not roll.
glAccounts: All balance sheet and P&L accounts (period lock)
gaap: ASC 855 — subsequent events recorded in the correct period, not backdated
redFlags: Books closed before all subledger summaries were closed
Books reopened without an approval trail
Books left open more than one month behind the current period

scr_gl_closing_books_from_the_g_l_workbe.purpose: Closes books directly from the G/L Workbench, which lists books and their status by entity, so the accounting manager can close several entities or books (accrual, cash, GAAP) in one place during the close.
scr_gl_closing_books_from_the_g_l_workbe.outcome: Faster, portfolio-wide period locking with the open or closed status of each book visible alongside other close tasks.
scr_gl_closing_books_from_the_g_l_workbe.rootCause: Large portfolios have hundreds of entities; closing books one entity at a time is slow and easy to miss. The workbench provides a single view to confirm every entity is locked by the reporting deadline.
scr_gl_closing_books_from_the_g_l_workbe.ifSkipped: Some entities stay open after reporting, allowing later postings into reported periods and inconsistencies between entities in consolidated reports.
gaap: ASC 810 — consistent period-end cutoff for consolidated entities
redFlags: Some entities closed while others remain open for the same reporting period
GAAP or tax books left open indefinitely

scr_gl_duplicate_je.purpose: The curated workflow for cloning a complex, multi-line journal entry — monthly payroll allocation, mortgage principal/interest/escrow split, intercompany billback — into the same or another book so only dates and amounts need changing.
scr_gl_duplicate_je.outcome: Faster, error-free recurring manual entries that keep the same account coding, departments and descriptions month after month.
scr_gl_duplicate_je.rootCause: Many month-end JEs repeat with the same structure but different amounts (the servicer statement changes the principal/interest split monthly). Re-keying 15-line entries each month invites coding errors; duplicating preserves the structure while forcing a fresh review of the amounts.
scr_gl_duplicate_je.ifSkipped: Accountants re-key entries and introduce transpositions or wrong accounts, or they reuse last month's amounts without updating them.
redFlags: Duplicated entry posted with last month's amounts unchanged
Duplicated entry keeping the old date or period
Duplicated reference number (RealPage does not enforce uniqueness)

scr_gl_duplicating_journal_entries_to_ot.purpose: Copies an existing journal entry into a journal belonging to a different book — for example from the accrual book into a provisional or user-defined book — to model the effect of a proposed adjustment on the financial statements before recording it in the main book.
scr_gl_duplicating_journal_entries_to_ot.outcome: The accountant can show the reviewer or asset manager the 'what-if' impact of a proposed entry (such as a large reclass or audit adjustment) without changing the official numbers.
scr_gl_duplicating_journal_entries_to_ot.rootCause: Large or judgmental entries — audit adjustments, capitalization decisions, bad-debt write-offs — often need approval before posting. A provisional book lets the impact be reviewed in real financial statements rather than in a spreadsheet.
scr_gl_duplicating_journal_entries_to_ot.ifSkipped: Proposed entries are posted to the main book for review and later reversed, cluttering the audit trail and risking reported numbers changing temporarily.
gaap: Audit adjustment evaluation (AU-C 450 — evaluation of misstatements)
redFlags: Provisional entries mistakenly duplicated into the accrual book
Provisional books included in owner reporting

scr_gl_importing_vendor_1099_transaction.purpose: Imports updates to vendor 1099 transaction data — flagging which payments are 1099-reportable and to which box (1099-NEC nonemployee compensation, 1099-MISC rents, attorney fees) — in bulk rather than editing payments one by one.
scr_gl_importing_vendor_1099_transaction.outcome: Year-end 1099 totals per vendor are correct before forms are generated and filed with the IRS.
scr_gl_importing_vendor_1099_transaction.rootCause: Vendor 1099 settings are often wrong or missing at payment time (contractors set up without a W-9, attorneys not flagged). IRS rules (IRC §6041, §6041A) require reporting payments of $600+ to unincorporated service providers and all attorney payments. Correcting a year of transactions manually is impractical, so bulk import is needed before the January 31 filing deadline.
scr_gl_importing_vendor_1099_transaction.ifSkipped: 1099s are under- or over-reported, the IRS issues B-notices and penalties under IRC §6721/6722, and vendors receive incorrect forms.
gaap: IRC §6721/§6722 — penalties for incorrect or late information returns
IRS backup withholding rules (§3406) when TIN is missing
redFlags: Corporations flagged as 1099-reportable (usually exempt, except attorneys)
Reimbursable expenses and materials included in 1099-NEC amounts
Vendors missing TINs while payments exceeded $600

scr_gl_income_statement_report.purpose: Produces the property operating statement — revenue (gross potential rent less vacancy, concessions and bad debt, plus other income), operating expenses by category, NOI, and below-NOI items (debt service, depreciation, capital) — for the month and year to date.
scr_gl_income_statement_report.outcome: The primary performance statement in the owner package, which the asset manager uses to report NOI to investors and lenders.
scr_gl_income_statement_report.rootCause: NOI is the metric that determines multifamily property value (value = NOI ÷ cap rate), incentive fees and debt covenants. Owners need a consistent, GL-driven income statement every month to track it.
scr_gl_income_statement_report.ifSkipped: The owner cannot evaluate property performance, lender DSCR tests cannot be calculated, and incorrect NOI can lead to wrong valuation and distribution decisions.
gaap: ASC 606 / ASC 842 — revenue recognition for other income and leases
NAREIT / NCREIF NOI definitions used by institutional owners
redFlags: Capital expenditures appearing in operating expense lines (understating NOI)
Depreciation or interest shown above the NOI line
Negative revenue lines caused by misapplied concession or bad-debt entries

scr_gl_inter_entity_account_mapping_page.purpose: Defines, for each pair of entities, which Due To and Due From accounts RealPage uses when a transaction involves more than one entity — an invoice paid from another property's bank, pooled payroll, a shared vendor bill — so the system automatically generates balanced intercompany entries.
scr_gl_inter_entity_account_mapping_page.outcome: Every cross-entity transaction creates matching receivable and payable balances in the right entities, which eliminate cleanly on consolidation.
scr_gl_inter_entity_account_mapping_page.rootCause: Management companies routinely pay one entity's costs from another's cash (centralized payables, pooled payroll, corporate insurance). Each legal entity must remain self-balancing, which requires automatic Due To/Due From entries. Without mapping, the system cannot know which accounts to use.
scr_gl_inter_entity_account_mapping_page.ifSkipped: Cross-entity transactions fail to post or post to generic accounts, intercompany balances do not agree between entities, and consolidation eliminations fail.
redFlags: Entity pairs missing mappings, causing posting errors
Due To and Due From balances between two entities not equal and opposite
Intercompany balances between separately owned JVs that should have been settled in cash

scr_gl_prepaid_duplicate.purpose: Duplicates an existing prepaid amortization schedule to create next year's schedule when a policy renews or a similar prepayment recurs, carrying over accounts and structure while the accountant updates the amount, term and start date.
scr_gl_prepaid_duplicate.outcome: Renewals are set up quickly and consistently, with no gap between the old schedule ending and the new one starting.
scr_gl_prepaid_duplicate.rootCause: Insurance and service contracts renew annually with the same coding. Recreating each schedule from scratch invites coding inconsistencies and missed renewals; duplicating keeps the structure and prompts the new terms.
scr_gl_prepaid_duplicate.ifSkipped: Renewal premiums are expensed in full or sit un-amortized in 1310, creating a spike in the renewal month and a gap in later months.
redFlags: Duplicated schedule keeps the prior-year amount after the premium changed
Old schedule not ended, so both old and new schedules amortize in the same months

scr_gl_prepaid_journal_entries_list.purpose: Lists all prepaid schedules — original amount, amortization posted, remaining balance, next posting — so the accountant can monitor, edit, end or duplicate them and confirm the 1310 balance is fully scheduled.
scr_gl_prepaid_journal_entries_list.outcome: A complete inventory of prepaid assets that reconciles to 1310 Prepaid Expenses at month-end.
scr_gl_prepaid_journal_entries_list.rootCause: Prepaid balances are only defensible if each dollar can be traced to a schedule. The list is the working register behind the Prepaid Expenses reconciliation and the place to catch schedules that ended or were never created.
scr_gl_prepaid_journal_entries_list.ifSkipped: Orphan balances accumulate in 1310 with no schedule, and auditors cannot tie the prepaid balance to supporting documents.
redFlags: Schedules with remaining balance but no future postings
1310 balance not equal to the sum of remaining schedule balances

scr_gl_recurring_journal_entries_list.purpose: Manages journal entries that repeat on a schedule — fixed monthly accruals, recurring allocations, straight-line adjustments, fixed intercompany charges — so they post automatically each period until an end date.
scr_gl_recurring_journal_entries_list.outcome: Predictable, identical entries post each month without manual re-entry, reducing close workload.
scr_gl_recurring_journal_entries_list.rootCause: Many month-end entries have fixed amounts (e.g., a monthly asset management fee accrual or a fixed amortization). Automating them frees the offshore team for judgmental work, but they need an inventory so they can be stopped when the underlying arrangement ends.
scr_gl_recurring_journal_entries_list.ifSkipped: Accountants re-enter the same entries manually each month, or recurring entries continue after contracts end, posting expenses that no longer exist.
gaap: COSO 2013 — review of automated recurring entries
redFlags: Recurring entries with no end date for time-limited arrangements
Recurring entries continuing after a property sale or contract termination
Amounts not updated after contract escalations

scr_gl_rent_roll_report.purpose: Snapshot of every unit's status as of a date — occupied, vacant, notice, model/down — with resident, lease dates, market rent, lease rent, concessions and balances, used to tie rent revenue in the GL to the property's actual occupancy.
scr_gl_rent_roll_report.outcome: Evidence that gross potential rent, vacancy loss and concessions in the GL agree with the leased units, supporting the GPR tie-out and owner occupancy reporting.
scr_gl_rent_roll_report.rootCause: Rent is the largest revenue line and the most important value driver. Owners, lenders and buyers (in due diligence) rely on the rent roll; it must reconcile to the GL, or revenue is suspect. Differences reveal missed charges, unauthorized concessions or units leased off-system.
scr_gl_rent_roll_report.ifSkipped: Revenue misstatements go undetected, occupancy reported to the lender differs from the GL, and discrepancies surface in audits or sale due diligence, damaging credibility.
redFlags: Rent roll GPR different from the GL GPR
Occupied units with $0 lease rent (employee units or unauthorized free rent)
Units marked vacant with charges posted

scr_gl_reversing_a_journal_entry.purpose: Creates the exact mirror of a posted journal entry — in the same or a later open period — to cancel an erroneous entry or an accrual whose actual invoice has arrived, while preserving the original entry in the audit trail.
scr_gl_reversing_a_journal_entry.outcome: The original entry's effect is eliminated through an auditable reversal rather than deletion, and a corrected entry can be posted separately.
scr_gl_reversing_a_journal_entry.rootCause: Posted entries cannot be edited without breaking the audit trail. Reversal is the controlled way to correct them. It also underpins accrual accounting, where last month's estimate is reversed when the real invoice posts.
scr_gl_reversing_a_journal_entry.ifSkipped: Errors remain in the books, or users try to delete entries (destroying the audit trail), or accruals are never reversed and expenses are double-counted.
glAccounts: Any account on the original entry
gaap: COSO 2013 — audit trail over posted transactions
redFlags: Reversal dated in a different period from the correction entry, leaving one period misstated
Same entry reversed twice
Reversals of prior-period entries without assessing materiality

scr_gl_scheduling_an_automatic_reversal_.purpose: Sets a recurring journal entry to automatically generate its reversing entry in the next period — the standard treatment for recurring accruals such as monthly payroll, interest or utility estimates.
scr_gl_scheduling_an_automatic_reversal_.outcome: Each recurring accrual reverses on day 1 of the next period automatically, so the actual invoice or payroll posting replaces it without double counting.
scr_gl_scheduling_an_automatic_reversal_.rootCause: Forgetting to reverse accruals is one of the most common close errors. Automating the reversal removes a manual step that offshore teams would otherwise have to track for every property.
scr_gl_scheduling_an_automatic_reversal_.ifSkipped: Accruals stack up month after month, expenses are double-counted when actual invoices post, and 2020 Accrued Expenses grows with stale balances.
redFlags: Recurring accruals without auto-reversal
Reversal set to the wrong period (e.g., two months ahead)

scr_gl_security_deposits_multifamily.purpose: Reports security deposits held for each resident — deposits received, additional deposits, interest owed where required by state law, deposits applied at move-out, refunds and forfeitures — so the 2110 liability can be reconciled to the resident-level detail and the trust account.
scr_gl_security_deposits_multifamily.outcome: A resident-level deposit register that ties to 2110 Resident Security Deposits and supports trust account and state compliance.
scr_gl_security_deposits_multifamily.rootCause: Security deposits are residents' money, not the owner's. Many states (e.g., New York, New Jersey, Massachusetts, Florida) require segregated trust accounts, interest payments and strict move-out accounting timelines (often 14-45 days with itemized deductions). Misstated deposits expose owners to statutory penalties, often double or triple damages.
scr_gl_security_deposits_multifamily.ifSkipped: The deposit liability cannot be supported, move-out refunds are wrong, trust account shortfalls go unnoticed, and the owner faces tenant lawsuits and regulatory penalties.
gaap: ASC 405 — deposits are liabilities until refunded or legally forfeited
redFlags: Register total differs from 2110 GL balance
Deposits for moved-out residents older than the state refund deadline
Trust cash lower than the deposit liability

scr_gl_standard_je.purpose: The curated workflow for standard and auto-reversing journal entries — month-end accruals, reclasses of mis-coded invoices, sweeps and intercompany allocations — with the attachments and descriptions reviewers expect.
scr_gl_standard_je.outcome: Clean, supported, correctly reversing manual entries that pass onshore review the first time.
scr_gl_standard_je.rootCause: Manual JEs are where most offshore review comments arise: missing support, wrong period, no reversal, vague descriptions. A consistent workflow (calculation attached, reversal set, clear description) reduces rework and audit risk.
scr_gl_standard_je.ifSkipped: Entries are rejected in review, accruals double-count, and auditors select unsupported manual entries for testing.
redFlags: Missing calculation support
Descriptions without month and basis of estimate
Accruals without reversal dates

scr_gl_trial_balance.purpose: The curated inquiry for the trial balance and GL detail: confirm debits equal credits, review every account's ending balance and drill into the transactions behind unusual movements before financial statements are released.
scr_gl_trial_balance.outcome: A reviewed trial balance with abnormal balances and unusual movements investigated, which serves as the basis for every financial statement and reconciliation.
scr_gl_trial_balance.rootCause: Everything in the owner package derives from the trial balance. Reviewing it line by line (abnormal signs, unexpected zero balances, month-over-month swings) is the fastest way to catch posting errors before they reach the owner.
scr_gl_trial_balance.ifSkipped: Coding errors, abnormal balances and missing entries reach owner financials; reviewers find them later at greater cost.
redFlags: Accounts with abnormal balances (credit A/R, debit accruals)
Suspense or clearing accounts with balances
Large swings versus prior month without explanation

scr_gl_trial_balance_report.purpose: Standard RealPage report showing balances of all GL accounts for a point in time or period — beginning balance, debits, credits, ending balance — by entity, book and location, exportable to Excel for reconciliation work.
scr_gl_trial_balance_report.outcome: The period-end trial balance used as the starting point for reconciliations, financial statements and audit schedules.
scr_gl_trial_balance_report.rootCause: Auditors, owners and consolidation teams need the trial balance in a standard format. It is also the basis for mapping property GL accounts to owner charts of accounts when the owner uses a different chart.
scr_gl_trial_balance_report.ifSkipped: Reconciliations and financial statements lack a common starting point, and owner chart mappings cannot be validated.
redFlags: Trial balance run on the wrong book (cash vs accrual)
Trial balance not in balance because of an unposted or partially posted batch
Ending balances differing from the prior-month package's closing balances

scr_gl_unit_activity_report.purpose: Lists unit-level activity — move-ins, move-outs, transfers, notices, vacant-ready, down units — across locations and periods to explain occupancy and turnover changes behind revenue and turnover-cost movements.
scr_gl_unit_activity_report.outcome: Operational evidence that explains changes in vacancy loss, concessions, turnover repairs and occupancy in the monthly financials.
scr_gl_unit_activity_report.rootCause: Revenue and turnover cost variances are driven by unit activity. When the asset manager asks why vacancy loss rose or turnover costs spiked, unit activity provides the answer. It also verifies that move-outs triggered deposit accounting and final account statements.
